title: Sepsis in the surgical patient

header.contentArea: high-risk postoperative intra-abdominal sepsis, resuscitation and source control
guidelineVersions: NICE NG253 “Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over” (published 19 November 2025; updated 23 September 2026)

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee called to a surgical ward. A 66-year-old patient is day five after sigmoid resection with primary anastomosis and has new abdominal pain, rigors and confusion. The nurse asks for urgent review.
brief.task: Conduct an assessment and describe your immediate management, escalation and source-control plan. The examiner will provide requested results.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Identify a high-risk septic surgical patient, begin concurrent resuscitation and antibiotics and identify source control.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Treating sepsis as antibiotics alone while missing possible anastomotic leak requiring urgent senior intervention.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: I am worried about sepsis with organ dysfunction; I need senior surgical and critical-care review now while I assess ABCDE.

flow: ABCDE, full observations, NEWS2 and immediate escalation.
Suspect abdominal source; inspect wound/drains and elicit new pain/rigors.
Take cultures and lactate, start timely IV antibiotics and carefully reassessed boluses.
Discuss urgent CT if stable, and surgical/radiological source control without avoidable delay.
Reassess perfusion/NEWS2, explain urgency and hand over clearly.

grid.label: Recognition and escalation
grid.fail: Attributes confusion and hypotension to pain without urgent review.
grid.borderline: Mentions infection but waits for laboratory confirmation before escalating.
grid.pass: Recognises high-risk sepsis and calls registrar/critical care promptly.
grid.high: Allocates roles, sets reassessment schedule and senior escalation while treating.

grid.label: ABCDE / NEWS2
grid.fail: Fails to obtain respiratory rate or blood pressure.
grid.borderline: Performs partial ABCDE but omits NEWS2 or repeat observations.
grid.pass: Uses ABCDE, requests complete observations and calculates NEWS2.
grid.high: Interprets deterioration alongside NEWS2 and communicates concern explicitly.

grid.label: Abdominal source
grid.fail: Does not consider anastomotic leak after resection.
grid.borderline: Lists leak but does not examine or seek evidence of peritonism.
grid.pass: Examines abdomen, wound, drains and asks about symptoms; suspects intra-abdominal source.
grid.high: Distinguishes alternative sources without delaying urgent surgical assessment.

grid.label: Cultures and lactate
grid.fail: Starts no blood tests or cultures in an unstable patient.
grid.borderline: Takes routine FBC but forgets blood cultures or lactate.
grid.pass: Requests blood cultures, blood gas/lactate, FBC, U&Es, CRP and coagulation screen.
grid.high: Obtains cultures before antibiotics only if this does not delay treatment and uses trends.

grid.label: Time-critical antibiotics
grid.fail: Offers oral antibiotics at end of shift.
grid.borderline: Says IV antibiotics but gives no urgency or antimicrobial strategy.
grid.pass: Prescribes local-guideline broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within one hour for high-risk sepsis.
grid.high: Checks allergy, renal function, source and prior therapy; plans microbiology review/de-escalation.

grid.label: IV fluids
grid.fail: Gives unmonitored large bolus with no reassessment.
grid.borderline: Mentions fluid but not volume or repeat examination.
grid.pass: Gives isotonic crystalloid 250 mL bolus over 10–15 min, reassesses after each bolus and escalates promptly if not improving.
grid.high: Escalates a deteriorating patient at once; documents each response; treats 1,000 mL without response as the latest point for senior advice.

grid.label: Source control
grid.fail: Plans antibiotics and routine CT tomorrow despite suspected leak.
grid.borderline: Requests CT without an early surgical source-control conversation.
grid.pass: Calls senior surgeon early; arranges urgent imaging if stable and intervention planning.
grid.high: Explains not to delay intervention for imaging if unstable and source control is clinically urgent.

grid.label: Communication
grid.fail: Leaves patient confused and family uninformed.
grid.borderline: Gives vague reassurance without urgency or explaining intervention.
grid.pass: Explains suspected infection, urgent treatment and need for further assessment.
grid.high: Communicates uncertainty and potential reoperation sensitively without overpromising.

grid.label: Reassessment / handover
grid.borderline: Checks again only if nurse calls.
grid.pass: Repeats observations, urine output, lactate as indicated and structured senior handover.
grid.high: Anticipates critical-care support, ongoing perfusion assessment and immediate deterioration triggers.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It is probably normal postoperative pain. I can review after the ward round.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Nurse: He is newly confused and shivering. His blood pressure is 88/52.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Give him paracetamol and recheck his temperature later.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What do you want to ask about?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Whether he is eating and when he can go home.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Nurse: He has increasing abdominal pain and less urine.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will send a routine full blood count.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Would you measure lactate or obtain cultures?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Not unless the temperature stays up overnight.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Perhaps a litre of fluid without checking again.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Could this be an anastomotic leak?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would book a routine CT next week if symptoms persist.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Nurse: His wife is on the phone asking what is happening.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: He is too confused to understand, and I do not need to update his wife now.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will leave the nurse to monitor him.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I am the core surgical trainee. I am worried about sepsis in a postoperative patient; please call the surgical registrar and critical-care outreach while I perform ABCDE.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Nurse: He became confused during the past hour and has rigors.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Please give complete observations including respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure and consciousness, so I can calculate NEWS2.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: RR 28, SpO2 93% on air, pulse 126, BP 88/52, temperature 38.7°C, new confusion.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That gives a NEWS2 of 14 (respiratory rate 3, SpO₂ 2, pulse 2, systolic BP 3, temperature 1, new confusion 3). I will give oxygen appropriate to the target saturation and assess breathing and perfusion. I am treating this as high-risk sepsis.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Is the abdominal pain new? Any vomiting, changed stoma or drain output? I will examine the abdomen, wound and drains.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Nurse: Pain has increased over eight hours. There is guarding and cloudy fluid in the pelvic drain.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That raises serious concern about anastomotic leak or intra-abdominal collection.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I need IV access, blood culture, blood gas with lactate, FBC, U&Es, CRP and clotting; cultures should not delay antibiotics.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Check allergy and local antibiotic protocol, then give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within one hour of the high-risk assessment.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Give a 250 mL bolus of balanced isotonic crystalloid over about 10–15 minutes unless contraindicated, then reassess BP, breathing and perfusion after each bolus before giving another. If he is not responding, I escalate at that point; I would not give 1,000 mL before involving seniors in a deteriorating patient, because 1,000 mL without response is the latest point for senior advice.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Nurse: His BP remains 86/50 after the first bolus.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: This requires immediate senior and critical-care involvement. I will reassess and continue monitored resuscitation rather than give fluids blindly.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The registrar and consultant surgeon need to consider urgent CT if stable and timely drainage or return to theatre; intervention must not be delayed if the patient is unstable.

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: Am I going back to theatre?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: There may be a complication causing a serious infection. We are treating you now and the senior surgeon will explain the safest investigation and treatment, including whether another operation is needed.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will arrange regular NEWS2 reassessment, urine measurement and a structured handover of observations, lactate, antibiotics, fluids and suspected source.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This is a time-critical deterioration on day five after colonic anastomosis. I am initiating ABCDE now; please summon the registrar, consultant team and critical-care outreach, and document the time of high-risk assessment.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Nurse: He has been more muddled for an hour.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Please tell me airway patency, RR, oxygenation, pulse, blood pressure, temperature and neurological status. I will calculate NEWS2 and repeat it during resuscitation.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: RR 28, SpO2 93% air, pulse 126, BP 88/52, temperature 38.7°C, newly confused.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: He is haemodynamically unstable. I will use supplemental oxygen according to the indicated target, assess capillary refill and peripheral perfusion and prepare for critical-care transfer if he does not respond.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I want to know the operation, intra-operative findings, any previous leak concerns, drain output, urine output and new pain. I am assessing for peritonism, wound infection and other sources without anchoring prematurely.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Nurse: There is guarding; the pelvic drain has become cloudy and urine output is low.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The likely source is intra-abdominal, potentially anastomotic leak, until urgently assessed.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will send blood cultures now, venous or arterial gas with lactate, FBC, U&Es, CRP and clotting. Culture collection must not postpone first-dose antibiotics.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will check documented allergies, renal status and the hospital intra-abdominal sepsis antimicrobial guideline, and give appropriate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within one hour of identifying high risk; narrow therapy when microbiology and source are clarified.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: With his hypotension, I will start balanced crystalloid 250 mL over 10–15 minutes, then reassess lung findings, BP, peripheral perfusion and conscious level after each bolus before repeating. If he is not improving, I escalate then rather than working towards a volume; 1,000 mL without adequate response is where NG253 requires senior advice, not a dose to complete first. I will involve critical care early.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Nurse: BP remains 86/50 after the first 250 mL.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I am documenting non-response and prompting the senior team to consider advanced haemodynamic support while I continue bedside reassessment.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Please notify the operating consultant now. Source control is a parallel priority: urgent CT abdomen/pelvis if stable enough; image-guided drainage or operation as directed by the senior surgeon. Unstable peritonitis cannot wait for a routine scan slot.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Am I in danger? Will I need surgery again?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This is a serious change and we are acting urgently. We suspect an infection that may need a procedure; I cannot yet say which, but I will keep you informed and ensure the surgeon discusses the choices with you.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will provide SBAR: postoperative day five, new confusion/guarding/cloudy drain, high NEWS2 and lactate 4.1, antibiotics given/time, each fluid bolus and response, urgent source-control question and next review time.

failures.move: Fails to respond to profound hypotension and confusion
Delays indicated IV antibiotics in high-risk suspected sepsis without justification.
Gives large unmonitored crystalloid volumes to an unstable patient
Omits senior surgical source-control decision despite suspected anastomotic leak.
Fails to reassess after interventions or relay ongoing shock to critical care.

recovery.when: If you missed the new confusion and shock
recovery.line: I focused on postoperative pain and missed the new confusion and shock. I am recalculating NEWS2 and calling the registrar and critical-care team immediately.

recovery.when: If you asked for CT before arranging treatment
recovery.line: I asked for CT before arranging treatment. I will start indicated antibiotics and monitored resuscitation now, and discuss urgent source control with the consultant in parallel.

knowledge.fact: Postoperative surgery within six weeks increases sepsis risk.
NEWS2 ≥7 with suspected infection is high risk; clinical concern can override a lower score.
High-risk adult suspected sepsis: broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within one hour of first NEWS2 assessment.

Initial isotonic crystalloid bolus is 250 mL over about 10–15 minutes; reassess after each bolus and escalate a deteriorating patient at once. If not improved enough after 1,000 mL in total, get senior advice.
Choice of antibiotics should follow local guidance for a known infection source and be reassessed when results arrive.
Seek early relevant surgical or radiological review for source control and intervene promptly on senior advice.

recall.think: Post-op deterioration plus new confusion and hypotension may signal an anastomotic leak.
recall.say: “This is high-risk suspected sepsis. I am escalating now.”
do: ABCDE, NEWS2, blood culture and lactate, immediate indicated IV antibiotic, carefully reassessed crystalloid.

numbers.meaning: crystalloid bolus over 10–15 min, reassess after each; senior advice if no adequate response by 1 L total, sooner if deteriorating.

recall.trap: Do not treat with antibiotics alone or postpone sepsis care until CT.
recall.finish: Early surgical source-control decision, repeated physiology and documented SBAR handover.

sources.name: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management, NG253
sources.supports: Used §§1.2, 1.6, 1.8, 1.9 and 1.11, and the NG253 algorithm “Managing risk of severe illness or death in acute hospital settings with NEWS2” (NEWS2 thresholds, 1-hour antibiotics, 250 mL boluses up to 1,000 mL).

partner.opening: Conduct an assessment and describe your immediate management, escalation and source-control plan.
partner.actorBrief: Opening nurse: “He is shaking, seems confused and his BP is 88/52.”

reveals.finding: nurse says abdominal pain increasing eight hours, new cloudy pelvic-drain output, reduced urine.
RR 28, SpO2 93% air, pulse 126, BP 88/52, temp 38.7°C and new confusion (NEWS2 14, Scale 1, on air).
patient asks: “Am I going back to theatre?” No definitive operative answer is available at this point.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Candidate must reassess, escalate, and avoid a reflex unmonitored fluid load.
